title: Book One · Chapter 62: The Same Number
story:
After supper, Mrs Lan takes the brown envelope from a high drawer.

She puts it inside her cloth bag. Mum goes with her. Ronan may come too, if he stays beside them.

“Can Leo come?” he asks.

“He is having supper with his family,” Mum says.

Ronan wanted to show Leo the real number six. Now he folds the small map. He follows Mum and Mrs Lan out.

At the tea shop, the pot is empty. The side gate is still open. Behind it, a short path turns past a wash line. Ronan sees three doors, then three more.

The last door has a small white board above it.

6.

“It has the same number as ours,” he says.

Mrs Lan looks up. “And that is part of the trouble.”

Mum knocks.

A woman opens the door. She has a piece of red cloth over one arm. A needle hangs from a thread in the cloth.

“Mrs Gao?” Mum asks.

The woman nods.

Mrs Lan says her own name. She shows Mrs Gao the outside of the envelope. She keeps it in her own hands.

“Is this for you?”

Mrs Gao reads the writing. Her face changes.

“Yes. I paid for meals for Mr Han. He is returning that money. I waited for his envelope.”

“What meals did you pay for?” Mrs Lan asks.

Mrs Gao tells her about the meals. She says the amount of money too. There is a note on the envelope. Mrs Lan checks the note. Mum listens to Mrs Gao too.

Ronan cannot see all the words. The adults understand now. Ronan can see their faces relax.

Mrs Gao takes the envelope inside. She asks them to wait. When she returns, she holds a folded address slip.

“East Court,” she says. “The old way of writing it was not clear enough. And some words outside rubbed away.”

“People call our little street West Lane,” Mrs Lan says. “Our door is green too.”

Mrs Gao laughs once, without much joy.

“And both houses are number six.”

Ronan looks at his map. Both houses have the same number on his map. The number alone is not enough. They need the street name too.

“Do you have enough now?” he asks.

Mum puts a hand lightly on his shoulder.

Mrs Gao understands him. “Yes. This is for a few days of food and a bill. I waited for it.”

He is glad. He is also sorry that he asked in front of everyone.

Mrs Gao gives Mrs Lan the address slip to copy. She does not show them the money.

“Mr Han will want to know it reached me,” she says.

“We shall tell him,” Mum says.

On the way out, Ronan walks slowly under the wash line. A red sock touches his hair.

“Now we know her address,” he says.

“We do,” Mum says. “Next we need to make sure the sender knows too.”

Ronan opens the gate for Mrs Lan. He is not thinking about his own good work. He feels tired, but he is glad too. Mrs Gao has her own envelope at last.

At home, he writes EAST COURT beside the new six. Then he writes WEST LANE beside their own.

When Dad comes home, Ronan shows him both places. Dad puts a finger on each name.

“Which one are we?”

Ronan points.

“And which one needed the envelope?”

He points again. Dad reads both names aloud. Ronan listens, then points to each house. The two street names help him choose the right one.

The two names are longer than the numbers. Tonight he does not mind.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- checks the note＝核对纸条
- address slip＝地址纸条
- reach＝送达
- in front of＝当着……的面

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：needle＝针；thread＝线；bill＝账单；amount＝数额。

## 读句提示

**Mrs Lan checks the note.**

Mrs Lan／核对／纸条。金额由成人核对，Ronan只在旁边看。

## 理解问题

1. 大人怎样确认信封的收件人？
2. 两个六号为什么容易混淆？
